body:
Reproduced on macOS (Apple M3 Pro, macOS 26.6) with Godot v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf], and with a 4.7.2-stable build from source with symbols kept. Both forms below are still in 4.7.2. The second needs no GDExtension at all, and a null guard in `_gen_extensions_docs` doesn't cover it. This PR fixes both, tested at its head 5017b3b6 (results at the end).

### Form 1: the GDExtension loaded during the first scan (#111645, #111048)

1. Make a project whose `project.godot` only sets `config/name`.
2. Add one GDExtension that registers classes. I used [TressFX-Godot](https://github.com/ismailivanov/TressFX-Godot) at a5cc2b13 (its `.gdextension`, `bin/` and `icons/`, with the prebuilt macOS library).
3. Run `godot --path <dir> --headless --import` with no `.godot` there.

It crashes with signal 11 right after `loading_editor_layout`, in 7 of 7 runs (3 official, 4 from source). The source build's backtrace:

```
[2] HashMap<String, DocData::ClassDoc, ...>::operator[](String const&)  (core/templates/hash_map.h:559)
[3] DocTools::generate(BitField<DocTools::GenerateFlags>)               (editor/doc/doc_tools.cpp:452)
[4] EditorHelp::_gen_extensions_docs()                                   (editor/doc/editor_help.cpp:3087)
[5] CallQueue::_call_function(Callable const&, Variant const*, int, bool) (core/object/message_queue.cpp:219)
[6] CallQueue::flush()                                                   (core/object/message_queue.cpp:267)
[7] Main::cleanup(bool)                                                  (main/main.cpp:5259)
[8] OS_MacOS_Headless::run()                                             (platform/macos/os_macos.mm:1272)
[9] main                                                                 (platform/macos/godot_main_macos.mm:136)
```

The fault address is 0x8, so `EditorHelp::doc` is already null when the call runs.

- With `if (!doc) { return; }` at the top of `_gen_extensions_docs`: clean in 4 of 4.
- With the stock build, but the extension listed in `.godot/extension_list.cfg` before the first import (so it loads at startup, not in the first scan): clean in 8 of 8. That is the workaround we use until a release has this fix.

### Form 2: no GDExtension, an editor doc cache from another build

The same race also hits `load_script_doc_cache`. It needs only two different builds of the same version sharing `editor_doc_cache-4.7.res` (here the official 4.7.2 and one built from the 4.7.2-stable source).

1. Run a short headless import with one build. It writes the shared cache.
2. Run the first short headless import with the other build, on a project with no GDExtension (only a few `.glsl` files).

That second import ends with these lines (the `WARNING` only in the source build's runs):

```
ERROR: Parameter "singleton" is null.
   at: is_cmdline_mode (editor/editor_node.cpp:6618)
WARNING: A Thread object is being destroyed without its completion having been realized.
...
handle_crash: Program crashed with signal 11
```

- **Official build:** 3 of 3 crashed, exit 134.
- **Source build, null guard above included:** 14 of 14 crashed. These exited 0, because the crash report stops after `Load address`.

`is_cmdline_mode()` is the check at the top of `load_script_doc_cache`, so the deferred call is running after `EditorNode` is gone. With the build's own cache, or none, the same imports were clean: 15 of 15 official, and 25 of 25 from source (20 with its own cache, 5 with none).

### This PR, tested

I applied 5017b3b6 to 4.7.2-stable (it applies there cleanly) and built it the same way as the source build above. I tested it on the same machine, with the controls run right after it. "Clean" means exit 0 and no `handle_crash` in the log.

| case | with this PR | control, without it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| form 1 | 5 of 5 clean | 2 of 2 crashed (official, exit 134) |
| form 2, one import at a time | 5 of 5 clean | 2 of 2 crashed (source build with the null guard, exit 0) |
| form 2, three imports at once | 6 of 6 clean | |
| the build's own doc cache | 3 of 3 clean | |

- **Form 1:** every import got as far as the crashed runs had: it listed the extension in `extension_list.cfg` and printed `[ DONE ] loading_editor_layout`.
- **Form 2:** the import rewrote the copied cache (3,269,730 bytes against the other build's 3,269,501), so it went through the same regeneration that crashed without the PR.
